newsitem.title: CHINA: China Southern seen issuing 1.03 bln shrs in float.
newsitem.headline: China Southern seen issuing 1.03 bln shrs in float.

text.p: Guangzhou-based airlines group China Southern Airlines Co Ltd is expected to issue 1.03 billion H-shares in a global flotation of shares which will be listed in Hong Kong and New York later in July, analysts said on Tuesday.

Analysts said the H-shares would be offered at a price ranging from HK$3.75 to HK$4.75 each and the carrier would grant underwriters an option to require the company to issue up to a further 154.5 million H-shares to cover overallotment.
H-shares are the shares of Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong.

Out of the total offering from China Southern, 71 million H-shares are expected to be offered to the public in Hong Kong, 350 million shares are earmarked for the U.S. offering in the form of American Depository Shares (ADS) and the remaining shares will be for international placement in the form of ADS and to strategic investors.
Each ADS, to be offered at a price ranging from US$24.2 to US$30.65, will represent 50 H-shares, analysts said.
The public offering of shares in Hong Kong is expected to run from July 22 to 25 and the share price is expected to be fixed on July 25, analysts said.
Dealing in the company's ADS is expected to begin on July 29 in New York and dealing in its shares in Hong Kong is expected to commence on July 30, they said.
"The company will use the net proceeds to fund its purchase of new aircrafts," one analyst said after attended the carrier's presentation on Tuesday.
"Proceed will also be used to reduce debt," the analyst said. "Its debt to equity ratio is expected to be reduced to about 3.3 times following listing from 9.9 times."
Goldman Sachs is expected to be the global coordinator of the issue, analysts said.

Among the strategic investors, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd would each buy 96.9 million shares, or about three percent of the enlarged share capital, of the airline group, analysts said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd will take 32.2 million shares or about one percent stake, and New World Development Co Ltd will buy 48.3 million shares or 1.5 percent stake.
Tai Fook Group Ltd will buy 16.1 million shares or 0.5 percent and Goldman Sachs will take 32.2 million shares or one percent of the airline stake, analysts said.

The strategic investors which their aggregate shareholding is expected to be slightly less than 10 percent of the airlines enlarged share capital, are seen to have an undertaking of holding the stake for at least one year, they said.
Analysts said 79 percent of the group's business was from domestic airlines operation and the remaining 21 percent was from international.
"The carrier emphasised that the group would focus primarily on expansion of its domestic airlines business but it would also seek international present," another analyst said.

The carrier forecast its profit of about 880 million yuan in accordance with international accounting standard for the fiscal year ending in December 1997, up from 726.8 million yuan in 1996, 226.9 million in 1995 and 103.5 million in 1994.
It also forecast its turnover to reach 13.40 billion yuan for the year ending in December 1997, up from 11.39 billion yuan in 1996, 9.03 billion in 1995 and 7.59 billion in 1994.
